sections.title: Introduction
sections.extract: Quantum computation is typically formulated on complex Hilbert spaces. The existence of exactly four real normed division algebras, R,C,H,O, motivates systematic extensions to H (associative, non-commutative) and O (alternative, non-associative) [1,2]. sections.extract: We brieﬂy recall the standard (complex) formalism to ﬁx notation. A ﬁnite-dimensional quantum system is modeled by a complex Hilbert space H ∼= Cd with an inner product ⟨·, ·⟩linear in the second argument and anti-linear in the ﬁrst. sections.title: Normed Division Algebras
sections.extract: A (real) normed division algebra (A, ∥· ∥) is a ﬁnite-dimensional real algebra with unit 1, equipped with a norm such that ∥xy∥= ∥x∥∥y∥ ∀x, y ∈A, and where every nonzero element is invertible. A classical result due to Hurwitz shows that there are exactly four such algebras: R, C, H, O, with dimR = 1, 2, 4, 8, respectively [1,2]. sections.extract: The equivalence between the quaternionic and complex models is formally established by showing that any computation in one framework can be efﬁciently simulated by the other.
